candidates.attacker_control: Resource property names and values are stored repository data. Any party able to write to a resource (e.g. through the Sling POST servlet if they hold write permission on that path, through content packages, or through any application that stores user input in node properties) can persist HTML/script payloads (for example a string property containing an or
candidates.counterevidence_checked: I checked whether the renderer is disabled by default (it is enabled: DEFAULT_RENDERER_PROPERTY=true and metatype says 'By default the HTML renderer is enabled'); whether a more specific renderer/servlet would normally intercept .html (the servlet is explicitly the sling/servlet/default fallback); whether another layer escapes the output (HtmlRendererServlet only escapes ResourceMetadata, not property values/path/type; no XSSAPI/ResponseUtil.escapeXml call exists in this class); whether other Sling HTML writers do escape (DefaultErrorHandler, DefaultErrorHandlerServlet and POST HtmlResponse.doSubmit do escape via ResponseUtil.escapeXml, showing the omission here is inconsistent with the project's own pattern); whether a mitigating servlet filter exists (none found for text/html output encoding in this bundle).
candidates.impact: Stored/reflected XSS in a default, enabled, framework-level servlet: script execution in the Sling origin for any user who views the crafted resource (.html), enabling session/CSRF-token theft, actions with the victim's privileges, and (in the web console/administrative context) further compromise. Same-origin script execution also defeats the platform's XSSAPI escaping guidance for that response.
candidates.prerequisites: Sling default configuration: DefaultGetServlet active (it is an immediate SCR component with sling.servlet.resourceTypes=sling/servlet/default, GET/HEAD) and enable.html left at its default true; the target resource is readable by the victim and has no more specific script/servlet rendering it; the attacker can write at least one property on that resource (or the property is already attacker-controlled).
candidates.root_cause: HtmlRendererServlet writes repository-controlled strings into the HTML response without output encoding: printResourceInfo emits r.getPath(), r.getResourceType() and ResourceUtil.findResourceSuperType(r) raw (lines 104-117), and printPropertyValue emits property names and property values raw (lines 143-161). Only the ResourceMetadata value at line 107 is escaped (StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml), so escaping is inconsistent. The renderer is enabled by default (DefaultGetServlet DEFAULT_RENDERER_PROPERTY = true, lines 90-94, 138-139) and is registered as the default handler for GET/HEAD on resource type sling/servlet/default (lines 60-64, 164-167), i.e. it handles .html requests to resources for which no more specific servlet/script exists.
candidates.title: Stored XSS in default GET servlet HTML renderer (unescaped resource properties, enabled by default)
candidates.trace: GET /<path>.html with no resource-specific script -> servlet resolution falls back to DefaultGetServlet (sling/servlet/default) -> doGet selects HtmlRendererServlet because ext=='html' (DefaultGetServlet.doGet, lines 224-253) -> HtmlRendererServlet.doGet obtains r=req.getResource() and the ValueMap/Map adaptation (lines 49-68) -> render() iterates the property map -> printPropertyValue writes name + ": <b>" + value.toString() with no encoding for single values and array elements (lines 143-161) -> printResourceInfo writes r.getPath()/r.getResourceType()/super-type raw (lines 104-117) -> response is text/html, so the stored markup executes in the victim's browser in the Sling origin.
candidates.unverified: No runtime/test confirmation is possible here (tests are absent and execution is out of scope). I could not verify with repository history whether this is a deliberately accepted debugging behavior, an already-known CVE, or the specific snapshot ground truth; exploitability depends on concrete ACLs (who may write the property and who views the resource) which are deployment-specific. The array branch uses values[i].toString() and can also receive objects with attacker-controlled toString output; the resource path itself may be constrained by JCR name rules but property values are not.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') / CWE-116

coverage_summary: Coverage: source_scope reports 4630 model-visible files, 0 excluded by size/name/symlink filters, and notes that the same filters apply to B0 and P1; all src/test trees are absent from the snapshot, so no tests could guide or confirm behavior. I reviewed in depth the core Sling modules (engine request processing/error handling, auth/core AuthenticationSupport + AuthUtil + SlingAuthenticator, servlets/get default + HTML/JSON/XML/redirect renderers, servlets/post SlingPostServlet/HtmlResponse/AbstractPostResponse, servlets/resolver and resource collectors, resourceresolver path normalization + ResourceAccessSecurity, extensions/xss filter/API, commons/log, commons/fsclassloader) and spot-checked contrib security modules (contrib/extensions/security, hapi, sling-pipes, distribution, davex, fsresource) plus broad regex searches for traversal, SSRF, command execution, deserialization, XXE, SQL/JCR query construction, redirect validation and random/crypto misuse. Large areas (JCR internals, JSP/Jasper compiler internals, IDE tooling, OSGi/installer internals, samples, Maven plugins) were only searched or skimmed, not line-by-line reviewed.
limitations: No repository history, diff, patch, CVE/ground-truth metadata or external references were available, so I could not verify whether the unescaped HTML renderer corresponds to a known fix or whether it is intentional long-standing debug behavior.
No code execution, tests, or scanners were permitted; all conclusions are static source reasoning and were not runtime-confirmed.
Tests were stripped from the snapshot (no src/test directories), removing behavioral evidence about expected escaping behavior.
Absolute-line and cross-module inspection was bounded by tool output limits; minified third-party JavaScript in web-console resources produced noisy search results and was not audited.
Deployment-specific configuration (auth.require paths, enable.html overrides, ACLs) is not part of the snapshot and was assumed at defaults from the metatype/component annotations.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS via unvalidated JSONP callback in the health check servlet (HealthCheckExecutorServlet PARAM_JSONP_CALLBACK passed to ResultJsonSerializer, which concatenates the callback into an application/javascript response: HealthCheckExecutorServlet.java lines 233-235, ResultJsonSerializer.java lines 66-68)
rejected_leads.reason: Real missing-validation pattern, but the servlet is registered by default at /system/health which the code documentation describes as intentionally not Internet-facing, so reachability is weaker than the selected candidate; also could not be linked to a concrete fix in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: JCR-SQL2 injection by string concatenation of an unvalidated fqdn into a query in HApiUtilImpl.getFqdnResource (contrib/extensions/hapi/core/src/main/java/org/apache/sling/hapi/impl/HApiUtilImpl.java lines 127-132)
rejected_leads.reason: String concatenation is clearly unsafe, but the query branch is only reached when resolver.getResource(fqdn) returns null, execution is under the caller's own session (ACL-limited), and the module is an optional contrib extension; no strong cross-boundary impact established.

rejected_leads.lead: Remote script fetch + eval in Sling Pipes (PipeBindings.addScript: 'http' prefix -> URL.openStream then engine.eval, lines 96-118)
rejected_leads.reason: Requires write access to pipe configuration content and is by-design script execution for pipes; not an unauthenticated/remote boundary crossing.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal in FSClassLoaderWebConsole download/view parameters (new File(root + file))
rejected_leads.reason: Counterevidence found: both sinks call isValid(File), which canonicalizes the file and walks parents comparing to root.getCanonicalPath() (lines 311-323), so traversal is blocked.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect via AuthUtil/SlingPostServlet redirect parameters
rejected_leads.reason: Counterevidence found: AuthUtil.isRedirectValid rejects '://', '//', '/../', '/./' and unvalidated characters (lines 451-508); SlingPostServlet.getRedirectUrl rejects any URI with an authority (lines 309-321) and REDIRECT_WITH_SCHEME_PATTERN handles scheme redirects; RedirectServlet only redirects to a configured sling:target.

rejected_leads.lead: ReferrerFilter host matching treats allowed port 0 as a wildcard (isValidUriReferrer, lines 398-407)
rejected_leads.reason: Weakens CSRF/referrer checking in a non-standard way, but this is upstream allowlist semantics for default entries and no concrete bypass of the filter's own logic was established.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE-style XML parsing (urlrewriter DocumentBuilderFactory, contentloader TransformerFactory with xsl from content)
rejected_leads.reason: Parsers are fed from configuration/content-loading paths rather than a direct remote request, and hardening presence/absence could not be tied to a concrete injection point in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: Deserialization sinks (ObjectInputStream in JcrPropertyMapCacheEntry, SlingSettingsServiceImpl, installer PersistentResourceList, DistributionPackageUtils)
rejected_leads.reason: Either reads local/server-side files, requires pre-existing malicious repository content written by an already-privileged actor, or is protected by a validating ObjectInputStream (DistributionPackageUtils.getSafeObjectInputStream).

summary: The snapshot is the Apache Sling monorepo (4630 model-visible files, no test trees present). I reviewed the core request/auth/render paths (engine, auth/core, servlets/get, servlets/post, servlets/resolver, resourceresolver, resourceaccesssecurity, extensions/xss, commons/log, commons/fsclassloader) plus security-relevant contrib modules using targeted searches for traversal, XSS sinks, SSRF, deserialization, JCR query building, XXE parsers, path handling and crypto use. Most historical Sling hardenings are already present (DefaultErrorHandler XML-escaping, POST HtmlResponse template escaping, AuthUtil.isRedirectValid, FSClassLoaderWebConsole canonical-path check, XSSAPI getValidColor regex, ResourceResolution search-path check, resource resolver normalization of absolute paths). The strongest remaining source-supported issue is a stored cross-site-scripting condition in the default GET servlet's HTML renderer: user/repository-controlled resource property names and values, the resource path and the resource type/super type are written verbatim into an HTML response, and this renderer is enabled by default and registered as the fallback handler for GET/HEAD on any resource. One candidate is submitted; other plausible leads are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
